en: One fascicle of the Recitation Method for the Messenger of the Fierce Wrathful King Acala of the *Tathāgata-samaya*.
By the Kai-fu-yi-tong-san-si, Te-jin, Shi Hong-lu-qing, [Duke of] Su State...

The Imperially Enfeoffed Lord of Three Thousand Households, invested with the purple robe and posthumously honored as Minister of Works, bearing the title of Great Mirror and the posthumous name of Great Universal Wisdom, the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple, translated by imperial decree. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha...
He addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"I shall now, for your sake, describe the Unmeasurable Power Divine Messenger of Immovable Might,
who is exceedingly capable of benefiting and accomplishing all undertakings."
First, purify the mind, prevent the arising of afflictions, eliminate all distracted thoughts, and concentrate the mind on a single point.
First, prostrate to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
and through practices such as repentance, cause the three karmas to become pure.
Only then should one perform all ritual activities.
If there is a lapse in the dharma due to distracted thought,
the master immediately violates the samaya.
One should recite this vidyā three times each day to extinguish all previously committed karmic obstructions.

The mantra is as follows: *Namo satvārthakārebhyaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ | Oṃ vīraṇa mahākāravajri sata sata sarati sarasati traya traya vidhamani sampanjani tāramati siddhagale ya traṃ ye svāhā.* If one wishes to go to relieve oneself:
Recite the following mantra seven times and protect the five places of the body— the forehead, the two shoulders, the heart,
and the throat— with the mudrā of the vajra.
The mantra for scattering [the offering] upon the crown of the head is:
Oṃ ajarakhañjana-sādhye hūṃ phaṭ. This is easily understood. One should then perform the purification.
Having emerged, wash your hands and rinse your mouth.
Then proceed to the vihāra and, as before, pay homage to the Buddha and perform repentance.
Thereafter, with a pure mind, join your palms in *añjali*.
Pressing the two thumbs against the forehead, concentrate the mind and recite the samaya-vidyā:

*Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām | namo susiddhisādany-agre karuṇe ruruṇide | āvaye atimañje | namaḥ sudhāma-siddhadhāke piyumamha-kṛpīṭe svāhā*. Next, protect the body with the seal of the vidyā of peace (*śānti*).
Interlace the two little fingers internally and extend them from within the web of the thumbs;
keep the two middle fingers straight and erect,
and place the two ring fingers on the backs of the middle fingers.
Grasp the ring fingers with both index fingers;
by extending the two thumbs and middle fingers, it is formed. The mantra is:
[OṂ VAJRAKARMA HŪṂ].
Namo samantabuddhānām. Oṃ hara hara maṅgalye tathā hūṃ phaṭ. Next, the practitioner should purify their karmic obstructions.
It washes away the defilements of body and mind from beginningless time, rendering them pure.
There are two kinds of washing:
first, internal; second, external.
Internally, one gives rise to the four immeasurable minds—
loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity— toward all sentient beings, along with the pure contemplation of selflessness and so forth;
externally, one effects purification by means of water.
Then, having bound the samaya-mudrā, recite the samaya-mantra.
Next, using the vajra-mudrā and its mantra, purify all impurities.
With the right hand, press the tips of the fingernails together.
The remaining three fingers are spread and held upright like a vajra.
The mantra is: Oṃ ajarakanañcanda svadhā hūṃ phaṭ. Next, the empowerment of water and earth to purify them is explained.
First, wash from the waist downward, including the bath robe,
as well as washing the hands and rinsing the mouth.
As for the mudrā, first join the palms together.
Bend the two thumbs into the palms.
Grasp the water and rotate it to the right;
the same applies to the earth and the other elements.
The mantra is: *Oṃ cauḥ samanta-vajra-ṇatratā amuka-candra-mahāruṣaṇa sphoṭaya hūṃ hūṃ trāsaya trāsaya hūṃ traṭ haṃ khaṃ*. Having washed oneself inside and out, one’s body and mind become pure.
The practitioner should next perform the ritual demarcation of the boundary (*sīmābandha*). He should do so by forming a fist with the right hand,
grasping the thumb with the three fingers below it.
Point the index finger straight upward;
by rotating the mudrā clockwise, one establishes the boundary (sīmābandha),
and by rotating it counter-clockwise, one releases the boundary.
This also accomplishes the expulsion [of obstacles]. The mantra is:
Oṃ hūṃ maṅgala-samantabhadre bandha bandha vajra-ālini hūṃ phaṭ. Next, bind the armor mudrā (*kavaca-mudrā*).
First, join the palms together, bending the index fingers and ring fingers so they enter within the palms.
Then, extend and erect the thumbs and little fingers,
making them equal in size like a three-pronged vajra.
This is called the Vajra Armor Seal of the Invincible One.
The mantra is: Oṃ hūṃ vajramaye vajrakavace hūṃ vajra phaṭ. Having sealed the five places with this seal, one becomes armored.
Then, having bathed as one pleases,
next perform the consecration mudrā: interlace the left and right ring fingers and little fingers,
inserting them into the palms.
Then, form fists with the middle fingers extended straight upward and their tips touching one another.
Each index finger presses down upon the nail of its respective middle finger,
and each thumb likewise grasps its respective ring finger.
Then, one forms the mudrā and recites the vidyā-mantra for empowerment as follows:

*Namo siddhyādhipataye namas sarvatathāgatebhyo hṛtsvadhānāvayaraśmini prasādini siñcatu me bhagavati marajare svāhā*. Next, one should protect the body with the armor-mudrā (*kavaca-mudrā*) and perform the ritual bathing.
When putting on the robes, recite this vidyā:
Oṃ hūṃ svaṭaya sahe hūṃ rakṣa maṃ phaṭ. Next, form the vajrāsana mudrā.
By empowering one's dwelling place with this seal and mantra,
it becomes an indestructible vajra ground.
One should then visualize a vajra seat upon this very ground.
For this mudrā, extend both hands flatly with palms facing upward,
and place the right hand over the left.
Recite this vidyā-mantra:
Oṃ hūṃ vajrasani vaṃ hūṃ phaṭ. Then, with the mudrā born of the Tathāgata, [perform it] upon this vajra-seat.
Arrange and install the assembly of Buddhas and noble ones.
Empower them with mudrās;
for these mudrās, turn the left and right index fingers upward.
Crossing the hands within and forming fists, extend and point the two little fingers upward while reciting this vidyā:
*Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ āmaṇḍalavikaraṇadīpti arśe svāhā*. Having thus arrayed the assembly of noble ones, [proceed].
Using the seal born of the Tathāgata,
one should visualize the offering of *argha* to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the Buddha-uṣṇīṣas.
If one can constantly perform this rite of offering while reciting mantras, one will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Furthermore, visualize the Immovable Honored One abiding in his original position.
Offer the aforementioned consecration mantra and mudrā;
then, recite the root mantra twenty-one times.
Homage to all the noble assembly.
One should immediately employ the aforementioned boundary-binding mudrā and rotate it counter-clockwise to dissolve the established boundary.
Furthermore, having bound the samaya-mudrā,
one should immediately fix the mind and proceed to the vihāra to perform the usual rites of prostration and repentance.
Upon reaching the maṇḍala site:
Take the mallet seal and cleanse the five places of the body of impurities.
As before, perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*) and empower the *iṣṭadevatā* (honored deity), and then sit down in meditation.
Furthermore, employ the Seal of the Tathāgata’s Birth.
Offer the argha water while reciting the mantra of the principal deity twenty-one times.
Perform the empowerment as previously described and make offerings to the principal deity.
Then, sitting upright, one should stabilize the body and mind.
Thereafter, one should demarcate the boundaries, such as the wall-boundary;
first, one should demarcate the wall-boundary.
For this mudrā, the two sides of the hands are placed together with the two little fingers extended upward and touching each other;
the two ring fingers and middle fingers are bent and inserted into the palms.
Bend the second fingers (index fingers) so that they form a hook on the side of the middle fingers;
bend the two thumbs to press down upon the lower joints of the index fingers.
Place the mudrā upon the crown of the head and rotate it three times to the right.
This immediately establishes the indestructible vajra wall.
The mantra is: Oṃ hūṃ vajramaṇḍale bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ. Next, bind the vajra-net mudrā.
First, join the palms and bend the two index fingers and the two ring fingers;
cross them inward with the right pressing over the left.
Then, align the two thumbs, the two middle fingers, and the two little fingers.
Each head is formed by spreading them apart with the fingers.
Then, turning the seal clockwise at the crown of the head,
one accomplishes the Vajrajāla-prabhāsa, saying:
Oṃ hūṃ vajrasara-puṣpe muḥ hūṃ phaṭ. Next, bind the vajra-flame boundary (*vajrajvālā-maṇḍala*).
This flame-mantra is empowered by the seal (*mudrā*) and its majestic power.
Outside the vajra wall, on all four sides and above and below,
a great mass of fire blazes with light;
no obstructing forces dare to advance.
For this mudrā, the two hands are turned back to back with the ten fingers interlaced like a blazing flame. Recite:
Oṃ hūṃ vajrajvāle hūṃ phaṭ. Having thus completed the boundary-binding (sīmābandha):
One should consecrate the offerings of food, drink, incense, flowers, lamps, and so forth.
As for the mudrā: join the palms with all ten fingers slightly bent, so that the tips of the nails touch one another.
Place this mudrā upon the food and other offerings to be presented;
touch them and recite the vidyā seven times to perform the offering.
One will then be able to swiftly fulfill all accomplishments.
Furthermore, one should sit with the mind fixed in concentration upon this mantra and mudrā,
visualizing all the various flowers produced on water and land throughout the world.
Furthermore, various exquisite trees of flowers and fruits,
as well as rare treasures, *maṇi* jewels, and extraordinary fragrances from all the mountains and great oceans,
gathered like clouds to present offerings.
He then recited sublime verses (*gāthā*) to empower [the offering],
making this offering while in meditative absorption (*samādhi*).
The verses said:
By the power of my merit and the power of the Buddhas' empowerment,
may these clouds of incense and flowers pervade all Buddha-fields,
making offerings to all Buddhas and the great Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, one should again contemplate and present the five offerings to cause merit and virtue to increase,
so that the vow for *siddhi* may be fulfilled and the Bodhi of a Buddha be attained.
First, the mantra of the unguent (*vilepana*) is spoken:
The merit of making offerings to the Buddha can eliminate the evil poisons,
fevers, and afflictions within the practitioner’s body; when karma is purified, one realizes the light of Bodhi.
Next, the flower offering is explained: This merit supports the practitioner;
All defilements of the three times Are purified without exception.
The fruit of Buddhahood shall be realized Precisely through this meritorious karma.
The commentary states:
Next, the merit of burning incense is explained; it can cause the karmic obstructions and afflictions of this empowerment to be exhausted, as the practitioner cultivates meritorious deeds.
Hearing from afar of these skillful means, they all come together to empower [the assembly].
Fragrant clouds of the Dharma-body pervade the worlds of the ten directions as an offering to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. The mantra is:
Next, the explanation of the food and drink mantras:

Making offerings to the Buddha’s merit enables the practitioner To swiftly realize the three gates of liberation and forever sever the bonds of the three sufferings, Constantly sustaining the life-force of wisdom.
Regarding the realization of the three bodies in perfection, it is said:
Next, the lamp offering is explained; adorned with the power of its merit, it enables the practitioner to swiftly achieve accomplishment through recitation.
The wish-fulfilling fruit of bodhi, its radiance pervades the entire dharma-realm;
it can destroy all ignorance, karma, and afflictions of all sentient beings within the three realms. Thus it is said.
The five offerings mentioned above—ointment, flowers, incense, food, and lamps—each should be recited eight times.
This can cause the objects of offering to pervade the entire Dharma-realm like clouds; furthermore, one should perform additional consecration.
By empowering these articles of offering with the power of the vidyā-mantras,
they become truly substantial objects; thus, when offered to the assembly of noble ones and distributed to all sentient beings, all shall obtain their actual enjoyment.
Recite this mantra eight times. By the power of this empowerment, the mantra for fulfilling the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) is as follows:
One should further contemplate and give rise to a true aspiration.
Then he spoke these words: "By the merit of my practice, may these exquisite offerings reach before all the assemblies of noble ones throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
may they graciously accept this humble offering."
By reciting the vidyā and performing the empowerment, it becomes true merit. The vidyā is:
*Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ, sarvatrāṅkusumitavijarasi ve namaḥ sūte svāhā*. Next, one should further bind the fundamental mudrā of Acala.
One should then recite the root mantra three times;
this will cause the Noble One to be pleased and bestow blessings, so that one’s wishes may be swiftly fulfilled.
At that time, the practitioner should further contemplate with focused and attentive mind.
The external wealth you have renounced may well be trivial;
now you should further renounce your own internal wealth— your very body and life—
to make offerings to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of noble ones.
One should immediately make a vow, speaking these words:
"I humbly pray that the assembly of all noble beings will grant me great protection and empowerment,
and always sustain me."
Thus he made this request three times.
The Noble Assembly did not refuse his wish,
and he immediately repented of all his transgressions.
May the ten non-virtuous actions committed since beginningless time be entirely extinguished;
Furthermore, one should dedicate [the merit] again: "Whatever merit I have now cultivated through recitation and other practices, I dedicate it to all sentient beings."
Dedicate this toward the fruit of Bodhi. Recite this vidyā-mantra to empower it, so that the aspiration may not go in vain. The mantra to be recited eight times is as follows:

*Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ | Namo sudṛḍhamaheśvaravajrahī sarvahindukaratiṣṭha sarmira-ma-tara-sarmira-śadhamanama tiṣṭha śu svāhā.* Next, one should further form the aforementioned consecration mudrā (*abhiṣekamudrā*).
Having recited the vidyā and performed the self-consecration,
next form the Ākāśanetra mudrā to protect oneself and the deity.
For this mudrā, join the palms with hollowed centers.
Bend the tips of the two index fingers so that they reach the first joint of the middle fingers.
With the two thumbs held upright side by side, it is formed.
Recite this vidyā-mantra:
*Namaḥ siddhye nāvanate sarvatathāgate oṃ gaganacari gaganasamasarvadharmate svabhāva-juvala-namo 'gane svāhā*. Having recited the mantra and performed the mudrā to protect the body, it is complete.
Immediately, turn this mudrā upward;
with the hands held as if cradling something,
it becomes the mudrā for holding prayer beads.
Then, recite this vidyā to empower the recitation for swift accomplishment. The mantra is as follows:

*Namo vajramukhe sarvatathāgatebhyo vāgbhava-jvālā-viyogātmane tadyathā jvala-vidhamani-candrimadgibhigari-tathāgata-vijaye śitatarati hūṃ jvalita-teje 'nukāra-yaṃ kuru svāhā*. Next, bind the mudrā of the Arising of the Dharmadhātu.
One should empower oneself so that no obstacles arise.
As for the mudrā: with the left and right index fingers and the two ring fingers, bend them into the palms and hook their tips against one another.
Join the two thumbs and the two middle fingers so that their tips touch, then open them;
press this seal against the left arm.
Next, move to the right until the crown of the head and scatter [the flowers].
At each point of contact, recite this vidyā once. The vidyā is as follows:

*Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām, āḥ sarvatrāloke svāhā*. Immediately thereafter, one should again form the previously mentioned Ākāśanetra-mudrā and recite the vidyā seven times; this is also called the Family Heart-mantra (*kula-hṛdaya*). Having finished the recitation, one should then contemplate with focused attention.
The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas fill the void with vivid clarity;
the assembly of honored deities stands face-to-face before one’s very eyes.
Settling the mind and stabilizing the intention, hold the prayer beads in both hands.
Recite with a focused mind and at a slow pace.
Continue until you are utterly exhausted, performing as many recitations as desired.
Recite three times each day without interruption.
The number of recitations should reach a minimum of one hundred and eight;
once the count of the recitation is completed,
one should immediately recite the empowerment of the *Ākāśanetra-vidyā*.
Having tied and protected the rosary, place it back in its original location.
Next, once again form the root mudrā and recite the hundred-syllable mantra to consecrate oneself, thereby swiftly attaining accomplishment. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ asama-sama-samanta-dharmatā-tathatā-bhiti-śāsani hara-hara samāraṇa samāna-vītado-mahā-dharma-te sara-sara.
*Samvara hola hola traya traya gana gana mahāmala ṭakṣi jvala jvala nasāgale svāhā.* Having recited this hundred-syllable empowerment, [one should proceed].
Furthermore, one should visualize that the previously contemplated deities, Buddhas, and assembly of noble ones appear vividly,
gathering me in and remaining before my very eyes.
One should then once again present the various kinds of vast offerings described previously.
Having completed the offerings to all the holy assemblies seen in the sky,
one should further, with a sincere mind, perform dedication and make vows,
speaking as follows:
May all the virtuous deeds I have cultivated through my practice,
And the power of my recitations and empowerments, Be dedicated to all sentient beings so that they may escape the suffering of the three realms And swiftly realize supreme enlightenment.
Having performed the dedication and made the aspiration, one should immediately form the various boundary seals (sīmā-mudrā) previously formed;
by turning them to the left, they are released.
Then, one should again form the previously mentioned consecration seal (abhiṣeka-mudrā).
Interlock the two little fingers with their tips touching,
then recite the vidyā of Lamp Flame Tathāgata while rotating the mudrā counter-clockwise.
All the assembly of noble ones each returned to their respective pure lands.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ siddhye nāvanugatebhyaḥ oṃ hrīḥ*. Next, perform the previous three-samaya mudrā.
I pay homage to all the assembly of noble ones.
Arising from the site of enlightenment,
I shall recite and read Mahāyāna sūtras such as the Avataṃsaka.
One may wander at will for one's own practice.
When the practitioner eats food or consumes various medicinal substances,
they should immediately empower that food with this vidyā-mantra.
Recite the vidyā eight times, and then take it; no obstructing spirits will be able to cause harm. The vidyā is:
*Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ | Oṃ vālanadīti-jumaliṇi svāhā*. If the practitioner can constantly practice and make offerings in this way, [the obstacles will be pacified].
Every day, when eating rice, tea, medicine, and so forth,
one should leave a small portion remaining and place it in a separate vessel; then,
one should form the mudrā of the Noble One’s Original Sword.
Recite the mantra seven times over the consecrated food, then place it in a clean location and offer it with a sincere mind.
As for the mudrā: form a vajra-fist with the right hand.
Straighten the two index fingers side by side,
with the thumb resting against the side of the ring finger's nail.
The empowerment mantra for the upper vidyā is as follows:
*Namo samantavajranāthāya ṭha amukaghaṇṭa mahāruṣṇa sphoṭaya hūṃ trāmaya trāmaya hūṃ traṭ haṃ kham*. With this, one should offer food and drink to the Noble One.
This Honored One’s original vow is that,
out of great compassion, he shall sacrifice his own body to serve all who perform recitation;
his body appears like that of a servant, manifesting the mark of being one-eyed.
If a practitioner receives this offering of leftover food and does not forget it in their mind at every mealtime,
I shall constantly follow and protect them day and night.
He shall not allow various māras and vināyakas to create obstacles and difficulties,
but shall cause [the practice] to be swiftly fulfilled and accomplished according to his wishes.
When the practitioner sleeps during the night, [he should recite:]
One should first form the seal for purifying and adorning the chamber:
first, bend the back of the left hand and place it pressed against the heart.
Then, bend the right hand back;
with the palms of both hands joined together,
raise the mudrā and place it upon the crown of the head.
Then, having separated the two hands,
one should rub them down along the body while reciting this mantra:
NAMAḤ SIDDHYE NĀVANUGATA-NĀM SARVA-TATHĀGATĀNĀM MAHA-SAMAYA-JĀTE SAMAYARA MA-MATA-RAMA-TRALOKI KITA DHARMA-DHĀTV-ANTASANGATE SVĀHĀ. Having thus performed the consecration with purity:
He then joined his palms, extended both arms fully,
and placed them upon the ground at the crown of his head, facing toward the eastern direction.
He also extended his two feet and prostrated with a sincere heart.
While prostrating, he visualized all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, each residing in their own land,
and made this reflection:
I now relinquish this body as a servant to offer service and support to all Buddhas;
I only pray that you will accept me and have compassion for me.
One should perform the supreme accomplishment.
Having made these three requests in this manner,
one may thereafter sleep and rest as one pleases.
One should constantly keep in mind the appearance of light and form the intention to arise quickly.
Furthermore, the *Acalanātha-dharmapada* states that the Buddha said to Acala: "O Messenger, Acala..."
It is capable of benefiting and accomplishing all undertakings.
If a practitioner wishes to practice and perform various rites,
they must first recite the dharma-mantra one hundred thousand times.
Then, on either the eighth or fifteenth day of the month,
perform a great offering for one day and one night.
Before the image, burn one thousand and eight pieces of *kṛtavedhana* wood mixed with clarified butter.
Recite once for each piece and burn them until one thousand and eight repetitions are complete;
thereafter, all rites performed shall achieve success.
Whatever words the practitioner utters,
all people will revere them and none will dare to disobey.
Should they wish to bind, strike, interrogate, command, or crush others, these things will all be accomplished according to their will.
Furthermore, on the day of a lunar eclipse,
one should take cow dung that has not yet touched the ground and smear it upon a maṇḍala according to its required size.
Upon the maṇḍala, scatter various kinds of mixed flowers.
Place a fascicle of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra in the center of the maṇḍala.
Take a tablet of pure color and ghee from a mother cow, and place them in a single circle within a vessel of refined copper.
Take *khadira* wood as large as a tooth-stick and twelve finger-widths long, and stir it [into the water].
Before the maṇḍala, perform recitation as if maintaining the mantra without limit to the number of repetitions,
until the three signs appear.
When the eclipse has ended, one should immediately cease.
Furthermore, having constructed a maṇḍala upon a mountain peak, one should fast and perform recitation until it reaches one hundred thousand times;
then, one will see all the hidden treasures within the earth.
Furthermore, there is a method: take milk and pour it into the fire continuously while performing *homa* and recitation for one thousand times;
this can eliminate pestilential diseases.
Furthermore, taking *kūlū* grass mixed with ghee, milk, honey, and so forth,
one should offer it into the fire by burning it one hundred thousand times;
this can eliminate great epidemics.
Furthermore, there is a method: take lotus flowers and mix them with ghee, curd, and honey;
offer them into the fire while reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.
The goddess Padmaśrī and others will be able to grant the fulfillment of one's wishes.
Furthermore, by entering the water at the mouth of a river until it reaches one's chest and reciting [the mantra] three hundred thousand times, one obtains *vīśaya*.
Moreover, by taking various flowers and casting them into a fire,
one obtains clothing according to the color of the flowers.
Burn seeds of the five grains;
one will obtain rice and grain to enjoy as one wishes.
Furthermore, take wood of the bilva tree.
If one casts [the substance] into fire and performs one hundred thousand recitations while burning it,
one will immediately gain the love and respect of a *rāja* king.
Furthermore, take *bṛhatī* wood.
If one casts it into fire and burns it,
it will cause all people to feel respect and affection. If one burns a tooth-stick [with this substance], [the same result follows].
One will immediately obtain immeasurable servants.
By burning barley, one becomes a householder.
For each of the above recitations, ten thousand repetitions must be completed.
Next, the method for painting an image of Acala is explained: one should paint Acala upon a fine, clean cotton cloth (*kārpāsa*).
He wears a lower garment of vermilion-red color, with a single braid of hair hanging from his left side and a topknot.
With eyes gazing askance,
holding a sword in the left hand and a lasso in the right,
he sits upon a precious lotus flower.
With knitted brows and a wrathful facial expression,
he assumes the posture of Trailokyavijaya.
Having painted him thus:
Place this image upon the shore of a river or the sea;
construct an altar according to the ritual rules and install the image there.
The practitioner shall likewise wear red robes.
With a mind free from attachment, dwelling in tranquility, and subsisting by begging for food,
one should recite [the mantra] five hundred thousand times before the image.
Then, during the night, one should take ten thousand pieces of *jāmbūnada* gold.
Recite once and cast one [into the fire], burning it within the flames.
When the number is complete, Acala himself will manifest his form;
the practitioner's vows will be fulfilled and all undertakings will achieve accomplishment.
The practitioner becomes a messenger of the Tathāgata themselves,
realizing samādhi and attaining a station equal to that of all bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, if they wish to subdue all evil persons:
Take cloth from a śītavana charnel ground and paint an image of Acala;
use one's own blood to dilute and create the colors for the image.
Place the image facing west.
The practitioner sits facing east and performs recitation.
Each day, at the three periods [of dawn, noon, and dusk], they bathe and put on wet clothes.
Once ten thousand recitations have been completed before the image, [the rite is concluded].
Then all that is undertaken will be accomplished accordingly.
Furthermore, one should daily offer food to all ghosts and spirits.
Another method is on the eighth night of the dark fortnight.
In a cremation ground, one should take a human corpse of a mother and sit upon it;
by reciting the mantra ten thousand times,
that human corpse will immediately move its ears.
"You must not be afraid.
He then opened his mouth, and a large, fully blossomed lotus flower emerged;
[the man] immediately seized it.
It enables one’s own body to become like that of a sixteen-year-old youth,
with hair like lotus rings,
ascending into the air to roam through the Brahma heavens.
One shall attain the status of a Great Vidyārāja.
Furthermore, one should recite before the image three times each day,
making offerings according to one's means and burning aloeswood incense.
Thus, having made offerings for a full six months with uninterrupted sincerity,
one will immediately attain the state of *viśalyā*. Furthermore,
there is a method for causing the enemy's military ranks to be broken and dispersed.
Consecrate one's own army's banners ten times,
and holding them, go out before the army;
that enemy host will be shattered, dispersed, and retreat in flight.
Furthermore, if one wishes to restrain an opposing army and prevent its ranks from moving,
one should paint the immovable Vidyārāja upon one's own banner;
he has four faces and four arms, and his body is yellow in color.
With fangs protruding from above and below, he assumes a state of great wrath, anger, and terror;
with flames blazing from his entire body, he manifests the martial power of celestial soldiers.
The practitioner displays this banner to that host of troops.
Furthermore, one should visualize the Noble One binding that host of soldiers with a noose,
so that the entire army becomes completely unable to move.
Moreover, regarding the method for causing the enemy forces to fight among themselves, quarrel, and retreat in dispersal:
Take the feathers of an old crow, an owl, a hawk, and a pigeon;
recite the vidyā-mantra over them while empowering them, and cast them into fire, burning them one thousand times.
Then that host of troops will immediately engage in mutual strife and contention.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause a *śatru* (enemy) who is at the point of death to abandon their life,
one should take rice husks, empower them by reciting the mantra,
and cast them into a fire while visualizing that *śatru*.
Bound with ropes by the messengers, they were led toward the south; overcome by agony, they spat blood and died.
Such is the nature of their kind.
None shall recover, and nothing whatsoever shall remain.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause the death of the commander of an enemy army,
one should take salt, soil, wax, and leaves of the *kṛtavedhana* plant.
Knead it together into a paste,
fashion it into that shape, place it upon the ground,
and recite the vidyā-mantra to empower it before cutting it apart.
He shall then die.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause an enemy army to become impoverished and deprived of provisions, one should take rice grains and empower them; they shall then become poor.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause an enemy army to submit and come [to surrender],
one should immediately form the Eye Mudrā of Acala,
utter the syllable *HŪṂ* with a wrathful voice, and [proceed].
If one visualizes the Noble One commanding the spirits and ghosts to seize and bind [the target] and bring them forth,
they will immediately surrender of their own accord.
Furthermore, there is a method for causing those who are greatly fond [of someone] to feel so.
Fashion that form out of seven kinds of salt,
break it into pieces, and perform recitation for seven full days;
she will then become enamored.
Furthermore, by taking kusuma flowers and reciting the vidyā one hundred thousand times while burning them,
a yakṣiṇī will come; whatever is sought among the three matters shall all be obtained.
Furthermore, take a mandārava flower,
recite the name of that person while performing empowerment,
and it will immediately cause them to become agitated and distraught.
Furthermore, by taking salt, consecrating it with mantras, and burning it,
one will cause a celestial maiden to come and serve one according to one's wishes.
Moreover, by consecrating and burning guggulu incense, [the same result is achieved].
One will immediately be remembered by kings and ministers.
Furthermore, he taught the method for painting an image:
in the center, one should paint Śākyamuni Buddha.
On the left, paint the youth Mañjuśrī;
on the right, paint the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
with a smiling face and holding a vajra in his hand.
Below Vajradhara, paint the Honored One Acala,
adorned with various ornaments;
then recite [the mantra] five hundred thousand times before this image.
Thereafter, all undertakings will be accomplished according to one's wishes.
Furthermore, there is a method: take the ashes from a cremation, recite the vidyā over them seven times, and give them to that person; they will immediately become enamored with you.
Furthermore, there is a method: take cow bezoar and empower it seven times.
By applying it to one's own forehead, all who see one will feel deep respect and reverence.
The Vināyakas will be unable to harm one whose accomplishment is blazingly intense.
Furthermore, by arranging the luminous Brahma-syllables upon one's own body,
those hosts of rākṣasas who create obstacles [will be subdued].
Within a hundred yojanas, all [evil spirits] shall retreat and disperse.
Furthermore, if a person is bitten by a snake or a water-dragon and does not recover after six months, [this rite should be performed].
Recite the vidyā-mantra to empower it,
draw the sword-seal (khaḍga-mudrā) upon his upper arm,
and appoint him.
Furthermore, there is a method: draw the great serpent Lūka coiled around a sword,
with flames encircling the sword.
Recite the vidyā-mantra one thousand times with empowerment;
when shown to the patient, it will immediately speak of itself.
If one recites the empowerment mantra one hundred and eight times for the patient...
One will thus always receive the protection of the Noble One.
If one daily consecrates the remains of the meal and places them in a clean location as an offering to the messenger,
one’s wishes will always be fulfilled.
Furthermore, according to another method, if there is unseasonable rain,
the practitioner, with a mind of wrath, should loudly utter the syllable HŪṂ;
the evil clouds will then retreat and disperse.
Furthermore, take thorns and cast them into a fire together with *harītakī* oil that has been consecrated;
this can stop heavy rain.
This also causes the practitioner to achieve great protection and accomplishes all ritual activities. Furthermore,
according to another method, one should paint the Vidyārāja Acala wearing garments of vermilion color.
With a single braid of hair hanging down on the left and eyes gazing askance,
he has the form of a youth;
his right hand holds a vajra at his heart.
Holding a precious staff in his left hand,
with slightly reddened eyes, he sits upon a lotus flower;
he has an expression of wrath, and flames emanate from his entire body.
Before the image, bind the mudrā of one’s chosen deity and perform recitation;
all things will be accomplished. Perform the recitation according to the previous method.
One ascends into the sky, becomes invisible, and all objects of desire are accomplished according to one's wishes.
This applies even if there is no painted image.
Whether dwelling alone in a quiet and secluded place, within a monastery,
or in a mountain cave away from the clamor of crowds,
one will achieve success in all matters and dharmas sought.
Furthermore, there is a method for empowering [a mantra] to cause a malarial patient to bind themselves and speak out.
Moreover, by empowering a mirror,
the Noble One appears within it and speaks of all matters when questioned.
Furthermore, take a boy or a girl,
have them bathe thoroughly and dress in fresh, clean garments, and place them within the maṇḍala.
Summon the Noble One to enter the maṇḍala and bestow his empowerment.
By questioning this youth, one obtains all matters.
Furthermore, if one wishes to accomplish the Kīlakarma rite,
on the first day of the waxing moon at midday:
Before the image, offer various kinds of incense and flowers as worship;
recite the vidyā-mantra one hundred and eight times without ceasing,
while visualizing that all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas within the maṇḍala are receiving you with compassion.
Recite the mantra in this manner every day for one full month.
Furthermore, take *kālānusāri* wood and *arka* wood, and smear them with clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
Consecrate white mustard seeds with mantras and cast them into the fire.
From the hour of Xu (7–9 p.m. until Zi (11 p.m.–1 a.m.), and continuing through the hour of Yin (3–5 a.m.), Kālarātri will come and speak to the practitioner, saying:
"What task shall I perform for you?
"I will accept it. Thereafter, she will always follow whatever the practitioner intends her to do.
He attended to his needs by providing whatever was required, such as food, drink, tooth-sticks, and pure water,
remaining constantly at his side;
he even went so far as to ascend to the heavens to fetch celestial maidens for him.
Furthermore, he will also explain the future [teachings], as well as the root mudrās, mantras, and so forth.
Regarding those root mudrās:
Interlace the two middle fingers inward to form a hook;
place the two index fingers side by side touching each other;
and with the two thumbs, press down upon the nails of their respective ring fingers. This is called "Ming" (Manifest).

Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ hūṃ vikṛta-vikarāla-mahābhairava iṣṭa-kṣiṇu sarva-kṣetra-hara-āntaramāra-dharāja-druka-jvala-bilura-dehi śa hūṃ vajra-gra hūṃ phaṭ. Next, the heart-seal (hṛdaya-mudrā) is explained.
Interlace the two little fingers and the two ring fingers with their tips facing inward.
Hold the two middle fingers upright with their tips touching each other.
Bend the two index fingers over the middle fingers so that they form hooks.
Placing both thumbs side-by-side and pressing upon the middle joints of the middle fingers, it is said:
*NAMAḤ SAMANTAVAJRANĀTATRĀ AMUKA-CANDRA-MAHĀ-RUṢANA-SAPHATA YA HŪM TRĀMAYA TRĀMAYA HŪM TRĀT HAṂ KHAṂ*. Next, the sword mudrā (*khaḍga-mudrā*) is explained.
With the left hand, the thumb presses upon the nails of the ring finger and little finger,
while the middle two fingers are held straight.
Insert the middle two fingers of the right hand into the left palm and clench them into a fist.
With the right hand, place the ring finger, middle finger, and thumb so that they press upon the nail of [the left thumb].
It is also said that the left index finger is bent to form a ring-like shape around the thumb; this is called the "Bright Day" (*vimalā*) mudrā.
Oṃ vajrarāga buddhacittaka hūṃ hūṃ kha hi kha hi īṃ ūṃ hrīṃ hāri viśvasattvān hṛdaya phaṭ āryarāgāñcaka-kiṃjirāya-si īṃ kaṃkariya kuru namaḥ svāhā. Next, explain the seal of the vajra.
With the thumb of the right hand, pinch the nail of the index finger as if forming a ring;
extend the remaining three fingers. This is also called the Seal for Accomplishing All Activities. The mantra is: [mantra].
Namo samantavajrāya oṃ ajara-kājaru-sādha hūṃ phaṭ. Next, the mudrā of the Jewel Mountain is taught.
Interlace the ten fingers of both hands with the palms facing inward and clench them into fists.
Next, the head mudrā is explained.
With the left hand, grasp the thumb with the four fingers to form a fist and place it upon the head.
Next, the mudrā for hanging down the braided hair is explained.
Interlace the two ring fingers with their tips facing inward;
join the tips of the two middle fingers vertically on their sides;
and with each of the two index fingers, pinch the upper part of the middle finger nails.
Place both thumbs between the ring fingers and little fingers with the nails joined back-to-back.
Join the two little fingers and hold them upright; by placing the seal upon the head at the corners, it is completed.
Furthermore, using this mudrā,
turn the head inward until it hangs down,
and place it upon the forehead.
This constitutes the Eye Seal of the Noble One.
Next, the Oral Seal is explained:
interlace the two little fingers with their tips inward.
Grasp it with the two ring fingers;
let the sides of the two middle fingers touch one another;
and let each of the two index fingers press down upon the nail of its respective middle finger.
The two thumbs point outward and are placed upright upon the mouth.
Next, the *kavaca-mudrā* (armor seal) is explained:
join the palms, and place the backs of the two index fingers and the two ring fingers against each other.
Join the two thumbs, the two middle fingers, and the two little fingers, then spread them apart.
Next, the Lion’s Vigorous Display Mudrā (siṃhavijṛmbhita-mudrā) is explained:
first, join [the hands].
With the ring fingers and middle fingers bent into the palms with their backs touching,
the two index fingers are bent behind the middle fingers like hooks;
the two thumbs and the two little fingers are each extended straight outward, side by side.
He immediately rose and performed the *vinardita* (yawning) gesture free from heat,
circumambulated the mandala, and walked its path.
Next, he taught the *jvālāmudrā* (flame seal).
Bend the right thumb and press it against the middle finger; keep the remaining three fingers straight and upright,
with their tips touching the palm of the right hand.
Spread the five fingers of the right hand apart.
Next, the *jvālā-nirodha-mudrā* (flame-subduing seal) is explained:
form fists with both hands.
The two thumbs emerge from between the index fingers,
and the fists are joined together.
Next, the śaṅkha-mudrā is explained.
Interlace the two little fingers inside;
touch the tips of the two middle fingers and the two ring fingers together;
extend the left index finger straight and place it against the back of the middle finger.
Bend the right index finger to press against the upper joint of the middle finger;
each of the two thumbs presses against the ring fingers.
These are the various mudrās from the Jewel Mountain downward.
Take a mantra from within your own family that you hold dear;
if you empower it and employ it, accomplishment will surely be realized.
Next, the *pāśamudrā* (noose seal) is explained.
Form vajra-fists with both hands.
Extend the index fingers of each hand;
insert the right index finger into the left palm and grasp it.
Forming the vertical mudrā at the heart, recite the empowerment mantra:
*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām apakārṣaṇa hūṃ phaṭ*. *The Ritual for the Recitation of the Messenger of the Fierce Wrathful King Acala Tathāgata Samaya*, one fascicle.
